title: kate-ui: count a tab stop in a wrapped line
summary: visual_row_count advances a tab to the next multiple of tab_width. A width of 0 counts as 1. The test goes in the existing layout tests module.

lane.reason: A local Qwen3.8 coder model with 27B parameters on the owner Mac codes this packet. The change is one file and stays under about 60 lines.

definitions.definition:
#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
pub(crate) fn visual_row_count(line: &str, columns: u32, tab_width: u8) -> u32

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: layout.rs has one test module named tests.  Add the new test function at the end of that module, before its closing brace. Do not write a second mod tests. Do not add a second module with the same name. Change visual_row_count to take tab_width: u8 after columns. Keep the dead_code attribute. A column count of 0 returns 1. An empty line returns 1. Let step be tab_width.max(1) as u32. Walk each scalar. A tab adds step minus the current width modulo step. Every other scalar adds 1. Use saturating_add. The row count is width.div_ceil(columns). Return at least 1. Update the four calls in visual_row_count_splits_a_long_line. Pass 4 as tab_width. visual_row_count of abcdef, 4, 4 stays 2. visual_row_count of an empty string, 4, 4 stays 1. visual_row_count of abcdef, 0, 4 stays 1. visual_row_count of four e-acute scalars, 4, 4 stays 1. Do not touch visible_line_range, span_line_window, notice_from, or the notice module. Add a_tab_uses_the_tab_width in that same module. A single tab, columns 4, tab width 4 returns 1. Two tabs, columns 4, tab width 4 returns 2. The text a then a tab, columns 4, tab width 4 returns 1. A tab, columns 4, tab width 0 returns 1. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip. Keep the change under about 60 lines.

regression_tests.name: layout::tests::a_tab_uses_the_tab_width
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main because visual_row_count takes two arguments. After the change one tab with columns 4 and tab width 4 returns 1. Two tabs return 2. The letter a and a tab return 1. A tab with tab width 0 returns 1.
